entries.scenePrompt: A single physical wooden cube assembled from identical small cubical blocks, viewed in TRUE ISOMETRIC projection, with the front and right visible faces equally broad and the top equally deep. Exactly TEN unit cubes span every edge: ten across, ten high, ten deep, thus a thousand units implied by the regular cubical construction. Each visible face is a ten-by-ten square lattice. Between the two outer boundaries there are NINE internal straight physical joints along each independent axis. Place a slightly darker continuous physical joint at the middle, after the fifth unit, making each edge countable as five plus five equal cells. Do not shorten the depth to seven or eight cells. All grids connect at the shared edges; all unit cubes have equal physical size. No detached cubes, text, numeric marks, counting ticks or decorative grid overlay. The visible outer dimensions permit counting; the interior is implied, not directly visible.

entries.scenePrompt: A blue physical cube assembled from exactly a ten-by-ten-by-ten regular array of identical unit cubes, in TRUE ISOMETRIC projection: front and right faces have equal projected breadth, and all three visible faces show ten rows by ten columns. Every independent edge has nine internal physical joints between its outer ends, giving ten intervals. A slightly darker continuous joint after the fifth unit divides each edge into two groups of five equal units, never seven/eight in depth. All joints meet at shared corners. Beside the large cube on the same ground plane, place one detached blue reference cube equal in physical size and projected edge length to ONE small unit on the large cube's nearest lower corner. No letters, numerals, arrows or grid annotations. The textbook convention gives each small unit a million, so the thousand-unit regular array relates to a billion; the textless image itself does not encode that unit convention or reveal the hidden interior.

entries.scenePrompt: Keep the current frontal bee, its four individually outlined wings, two antennae, striped abdomen and separate bubble. Correct the leg structure: the current bee has only FOUR independently traceable legs. Rebuild SIX jointed legs as three bilateral pairs attached to the hairy THORAX, with distinct origins and distinct clawed ends. The FRONT pair extends laterally and slightly upward into the space below the wing roots; the MIDDLE pair extends diagonally outward and downward; the HIND pair extends farther downward on either side of the abdomen while still beginning at the lower thorax, never the abdomen. Separate all six leg silhouettes so none disappears behind another leg or the abdomen. No disconnected extra limbs. Preserve the larger forewing and smaller hindwing on each side, with four wing outlines total. Do not add wings, text, labels, arrows or decorative markings.
